title: 8.4 Data Displays

icans: I can tell whether data are qualitative or quantitative.
I can choose an appropriate display for a data set and explain why.
I can read and interpret common data displays.

vocab: data that are labels or _____________, such as colors, names, or zip codes
numbers that are ___________ or counted, such as heights or test scores
compares the counts of _____________; the bars don’t touch
shows parts of a __________; each section’s angle is its share of 360°
shows how many ____________ values fall in each interval; the bars touch
shows the ______________ summary and spread of numerical data

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Qualitative data are _______________; quantitative data are numbers that are _______________ or _______________.

blocks.stem:
Tell whether the data are qualitative or quantitative.
a.  favorite colors of students        b.  heights of plants
c.  zip codes of customers               d.  numbers of pets owned

notes: Choosing a display: Categories with counts → _______________ Parts of a whole → _______________
Choosing a display: Numbers in intervals → _______________ Change over time → _______________

blocks.stem:
Which display best represents each data set?
a.  a city’s monthly rainfall over one year
b.  the percent of a budget spent on each type of expense
c.  the number of students choosing each lunch option
d.  the median and spread of the prices of 40 laptops

notes: Circle graphs: In a circle graph, a section’s angle = its share · ________.

blocks.stem:
The table shows the favorite seasons of 30 students.
a.  What percent of the students chose fall?
b.  In a circle graph, what is the central angle of the fall section?
c.  Name two good displays for these data.
You want to show how many of 24 students scored 60–69, 70–79, 80–89, and 90–100 on a test. Which display should you use? Why do its bars touch?
Tell whether the data are qualitative or quantitative: the number of text messages sent in a day, favorite type of music, area codes, weights of backpacks.

Choose the best display.
a.  your height each year from age 5 to age 15
b.  the votes for each candidate for class president

tickets.stem: Are student ID numbers qualitative or quantitative?
Are the ages of the people at a concert qualitative or quantitative?
What is the best display to show how a stock price changed over one month?
